Spatial predicates of polygons against grid cells

Source: R/relate_cells.R
relate_cells.Rd

Computes the DE-9IM intersection matrix of each polygon against each grid cell its boundary touches, from a finished burn() and the same geometry. With it, every cell's relation to every polygon is known: a cell the boundary does not reach is either wholly inside the polygon (it is in one of the polygon's runs: matrix "212FF1FF2", covered) or wholly outside (no record: "FF2FF1212", disjoint).

Usage

relate_cells(x, burn)

Arguments

x

the geometry that was burned (any input burn() accepts).

burn

the controlledburn result of burn(x, ...), in either mode and with any options. Only its runs, grid and id_offset are used. A result cropped with crop_burn() or sliced with slice_burn() gives the relations on its window's grid.

Value

A data.frame with one row per (polygon, cell) the polygon's boundary touches, sorted by id, row, col:

row, col

the cell, 1-based, row 1 at the top.

id

the geometry, as in the burn.

matrix

the DE-9IM matrix as nine characters, the polygon's interior, boundary and exterior (rows) against the cell's (columns).

intersects

they share a point.

interiors_meet

the polygon covers part of the cell's area.

covers

no point of the cell is outside the polygon.

touches

they share a point but no area.

covered_by

no point of the polygon is outside the cell.

Details

The cells returned include those the boundary only touches, along a wall or at a corner, which have no record in the burn. So an exact "all touched" set of a polygon is its runs plus the relations with intersects, and the cells it covers are its runs plus the relations with covers. Contacts are decided with exact predicates on the input coordinates, not from the burn's coverage fractions: the burn treats coverage within 1e-6 of 0 or 1 as 0 or 1, so a cell holding a sliver of a polygon may have no record, or be in a run, and is still reported here as touched or partly covered.

Polygons are assumed valid (rings that do not cross, holes inside their shell, the parts of a multipolygon meeting only at points). Lines, points and empty geometries give no relations.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("geos", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ## a square on cell walls: its 4 cells are covered, and the 12 around
  ## it touch it without sharing any area
  sq <- geos::as_geos_geometry("POLYGON ((1 1, 3 1, 3 3, 1 3, 1 1))")
  r <- burn(sq, extent = c(0, 4, 0, 4), dimension = c(4L, 4L))
  rel <- relate_cells(sq, r)
  table(rel$matrix)
  sum(rel$touches)

  ## exact all-touched cells of a polygon: its runs plus the cells
  ## its boundary meets
  poly <- geos::as_geos_geometry("POLYGON ((0.5 0.5, 2.5 0.7, 2 3.2, 0.5 0.5))")
  r <- burn(poly, extent = c(0, 4, 0, 4), dimension = c(4L, 4L))
  rel <- relate_cells(poly, r)
  rel[rel$intersects, c("row", "col")]
}
#>    row col
#> 1    1   2
#> 2    1   3
#> 3    2   2
#> 4    2   3
#> 5    3   1
#> 6    3   2
#> 7    3   3
#> 8    4   1
#> 9    4   2
#> 10   4   3
